reviews.content: This book gave me the tools and steps I needed to implement a plan for my babies to sleep well. My twins were waking suddenly every 1 hour (so do the math- I did not sleep). Since I don't believe in allowing a child to cry, I parented my heart out until I got very sick and missed their first Christmas being ill. After that, I decided to take charge!! Some of my Attachment Parent friends and one of my Montessori Professors (I got my M of Ed in Montessori)suggested this book to me. I read it all in one day- and highlighted the heck out of it. Then I typed my plan and made DH swear up and down he'd help me. We introduced lovies, ended nursing to sleep, and got them back to sleeping 11 hours straight at night within 20 days. I never had to cry----and neither did my precious sweet twins!!! You. Need. This. Book. Get some rest Mommas!!!
reviews.title: This book got me through nights with twins and a toddler!

reviews.content: This book is a great read for parents looking for a gentler solution to sleep training. I truly believe there's no one fits all approach to sleep training, each family is different with different needs. The downside to this book is that there's so many options it can be confusing for parents who are already sleep deprived to comprehend, and the process can be a lengthy one. The addition of the videos to go over each section is wonderful. It also is very supportive of all parenting types; whether you breast or bottle feed, or your baby sleeps in a crib or co-sleep Ms. Pantley covers it in a very non-judgemental way.  All in all I would recommend this as a  good read for parents who are looking for the gentlest way to sleep train.

reviews.content: I just couldn't stomach the thought of leaving my twin babies to CIO all alone, wondering why Mama didn't come when they needed me. . . I tried a few of the techniques in The No-Cry Sleep Solution -- gave each boy a lovey, used consistent ""sleepy time"" music and ocean sounds, watched for sleep cues like yawning, glazed eyes, etc. And a pretty consistent naptime and bedtime routine at about the same times each day. And they all worked well enough, gently and reliably. And my babies don't have to cry themselves to sleep alone in their cribs just so I can get more shut-eye. They are better, easier sleepers now thanks to the tips in the book-- though not perfect, because they're babies, not robots. And that's fine with me. . . they'll be far more independent sooner than I'll want, I don't need them to be self-reliant sleepers when they're 6 mos. old.
reviews.title: Anything's Better Than CIO
